title: The Weil fundamental representation is a continuous representation
statement:
In the situation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation], the formula

$$
\rho(\gamma s^n):=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma)T_s^n
\qquad(\gamma\in\pi_1(X,\bar x),\ n\in\mathbf Z)
$$

defines a continuous group homomorphism
$\rho:W(X_0,\bar x)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with
$\rho|_{\pi_1(X,\bar x)}=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ and
$\rho(s)=T_s$.

proof.text:
Every $g\in W(X_0,\bar x)$ has a unique expression $g=\gamma s^n$ with
$\gamma\in\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Indeed, the fibre
product of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] is formed over
$\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$ against the cyclic subgroup
$\langle\Phi_X\rangle$ of [def-tw-frobenius-action]: its
projection to $\langle\Phi_X\rangle\cong\mathbf Z$ is a homomorphism
whose kernel consists of the pairs $(\gamma,1)$ with $\gamma$ in the
kernel of $\pi_1(X_0,\bar x)\to\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, that is, of
the elements of $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$; so $n$ is determined by $g$ and
then $\gamma=gs^{-n}$. Hence the displayed formula defines a map, and it
extends $\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ (case $n=0$) and takes $s$ to
$T_s$ (case $\gamma=1$, $n=1$).

It is a homomorphism: $\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ is a homomorphism by the
lisse sheaf–representation equivalence of
[cor-galois-lisse-representations]; the commutation relation
displayed in [def-wf-fundamental-representation] rewrites
$\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(s^n\gamma s^{-n})$ as
$T_s^n\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma)T_s^{-n}$; and
$W(X_0,\bar x)$ multiplies as
$(\gamma s^n)(\gamma's^{n'})=\gamma(s^n\gamma's^{-n})s^{n+n'}$.

For continuity let $g=\gamma_0s^n$ and let $U\subseteq \operatorname{GL}(V)$ be an open neighbourhood of $\rho(g)$. The
subset of $W(X_0,\bar x)$ projecting to the fixed exponent $n$ under
the fibre-product projection to $\langle\Phi_X\rangle\cong\mathbf Z$ is
open in $W(X_0,\bar x)$, and on it the formula
reads $\gamma s^n\mapsto\rho(g)\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma_0^{-1}\gamma)$.
By the continuity of $\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ of
[cor-galois-lisse-representations] there is an open subgroup
$N\subseteq\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ with
$\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(N)\subseteq\rho(g)^{-1}U$, and then
$\rho(Ns^n)\subseteq U$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(W,\deg,s)$ be a degree datum ([d-monodromy]) with $P=\ker(\deg)$,
let $f:P\to M$ be a homomorphism to a group $M$, and let $T\in M$
satisfy $Tf(u)T^{-1}=f(sus^{-1})$ for all $u\in P$. Then

$$
\tilde f(us^n):=f(u)T^n
\qquad(u\in P,\ n\in\mathbf Z)
$$

is a well-defined group homomorphism $\tilde f:W\to M$ with
$\tilde f|_P=f$ and $\tilde f(s)=T$. If $W$ and $M$ are topological
groups, $P$ is open in $W$ and $f$ is continuous, then $\tilde f$ is
continuous.

In particular, in the situation of [def-wf-fundamental-representation],
the formula

$$
\rho(\gamma s^n):=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}(\gamma)T_s^n
\qquad(\gamma\in\pi_1(X,\bar x),\ n\in\mathbf Z)
$$

defines a continuous group homomorphism
$\rho:W(X_0,\bar x)\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with
$\rho|_{\pi_1(X,\bar x)}=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$ and
$\rho(s)=T_s$.

proof.text:
*The abstract extension.* By [d-monodromy] every $w\in W$ has the form
$us^n$ with $n=\deg(w)$ and $u=ws^{-n}\in P$, and this expression is
unique because $n$ is determined by $w$. Hence $\tilde f$ is a
well-defined map; it restricts to $f$ (case $n=0$) and takes $s$ to $T$
(case $u=1$, $n=1$). Induction on $m$, in both directions, turns the
hypothesis on $T$ into $T^mf(u)T^{-m}=f(s^mus^{-m})$ for all
$m\in\mathbf Z$. Since
$(us^n)(u's^{n'})=u(s^nu's^{-n})s^{n+n'}$ with
$s^nu's^{-n}\in P$ ($P$ is normal), we get

$$
\tilde f\bigl((us^n)(u's^{n'})\bigr)
=f(u)\,T^nf(u')T^{-n}\,T^{n+n'}
=\tilde f(us^n)\,\tilde f(u's^{n'}),
$$

so $\tilde f$ is a homomorphism. If $P$ is open and $f$ is continuous,
then $\tilde f$ agrees with the continuous map $f$ on the open
neighbourhood $P$ of $1$, so it is continuous at $1$; a homomorphism of
topological groups that is continuous at $1$ is continuous.

*The Weil fundamental representation.* By
[lem-wf-weil-group-exact-sequence], $\deg:W(X_0,\bar x)\to\mathbf Z$ is
surjective with kernel $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$, so $(W(X_0,\bar x),\deg,s)$ is a
degree datum with $P=\pi_1(X,\bar x)$. Take $M=\operatorname{GL}(V)$,
$f=\rho_{\mathrm{geom}}$, which is a continuous homomorphism by the lisse
sheaf–representation equivalence of [thm-lisse-qlbar-representations],
and $T=T_s$; the commutation relation displayed in
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] is the hypothesis on $T$. The
subgroup $\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ is open in $W(X_0,\bar x)$: it is the fibre
over $0$ of the projection of the fibre product of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation] to the discrete group
$\langle\Phi_X\rangle\cong\mathbf Z$ of [def-tw-frobenius-action]. The
first part therefore applies, and $\tilde f$ is the displayed $\rho$.
